Q-005.why: looks for an invented `decisions` effect; the declared subject is in t.instances[].subject

Q-007.why: /create/ also matches carrier.create, so every shipment counts as a second creation of the order

Q-011.why: reads "must be matched" as "an effect must follow every ref-less carrier message"; a repeated delivered report for a completed fulfilment correctly changes nothing (§3.3)

Q-018.why: attributes the original order's later effects (same subject, after the duplicate arrived) to the duplicate

Q-019.why: counts a duplicate order.placed as a "new order"

Q-021.why: anchors R2.1's reject on a review answer (R2.2's trigger) and wants an op named *cancel* whose args name "fraud"; no API op carries a reason (orders.setStatus takes orderId, fulfilmentId, status)

Q-024.why: demands a workflow timer whose kind matches /review/, an implementation choice SPEC-E never states (lineage 1 names its timers `timer`)

Q-025.why: treats "cleared" (a state) as an effect whose op matches /clear/

Q-027.why: wants "fraud-review-timeout" inside a cancel op's args; the reason has no API field

Q-031.why: turns "the first amend or cancel at or before D counts" into "every order must get an amend or cancel by D"

Q-035.why: wants an op named *cancel* with args.reason = customer; cancelling is setStatus + order-cancelled, with no reason field

Q-040.why: ignores go-live: migrated orders were recorded before go-live (migration payload), so their status changes need no orders.create

Q-041.why: compares a fulfilment's charge with the order's first reserve, not the reserve "of the same fulfilment"

Q-059.why: looks for an op named *compens*; compensation is carrier.cancel / billing.refund / inventory.release

Q-064.why: ignores whether the cancel counts (a cancel after collection is refused, R6.2/R6.3); reads an invented payload.counted

Q-072.why: keys a fulfilment's status by args.orderId (always present), so setting F1 and F2 to processing counts as setting the order twice

Q-003.why: the quote states platform behaviour (`after`), not a workflow obligation; the property compares an after-chained effect's emission time with its predecessor's result time

Q-014.why: the reference policy is oracle-informed and never emits the inventory.allocate read that R1.1 asks for; lineage 1 passes this requirement on 367/367 orders

Q-043.why: requires the resubmission strictly after the partial result (`>`); the reference resubmits in the same instant. Lineage 1 does too, and is `untested` only because it never closes the instance the window is tied to

Q-044.why: the reference charges at the commit instant, 1 s before the reserve result is delivered (it acts on commit times a real workflow cannot see); the property also groups reserves by order, not fulfilment

Q-045.why: as Q-044, for carrier.create after the charge
